question: The greatest number, which divides 2248 and 1761 to leave 3 and 1 respectively as remainders, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number is the HCF of (2248 − 3) and (1761 − 1).

⇒ Required HCF = HCF of 2245 and 1760

Since the last digits of 2245 and 1760 are 5 and 0 respectively, both numbers are exactly divisible by 5.

Checking the given options, only 5 perfectly divides both 2245 and 1760.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers to be divided = 2248 and 1761

Respective remainders = 3 and 1

**Formula Used:**

Required number = HCF of (N₁ − R₁) and (N₂ − R₂)

**Calculation:**

⇒ First Number = 2248 − 3 = 2245

⇒ Second Number = 1761 − 1 = 1760

⇒ Required Number = HCF of 2245 and 1760

⇒ Prime factorization of 2245 = 5 × 449

⇒ Prime factorization of 1760 = 2⁵ × 5 × 11

⇒ The highest common factor of both the numbers is 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF leaving different remainders

The greatest number that divides a, b, and c leaving remainders x, y, and z respectively is the HCF of (a − x), (b − y), and (c − z).

HCF leaving same remainder (known)

The greatest number that divides a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r in each case is the HCF of (a − r), (b − r), and (c − r).

HCF leaving same remainder (unknown)

The greatest number that divides a, b, and c leaving the same unknown remainder in each case is the HCF of |a − b|, |b − c|, and |c − a|.

LCM leaving same remainder

The smallest number that, when divided by a, b, and c, leaves the same remainder r in each case is given by [LCM of (a, b, c)] + r.
